howSpursPlayed: Spurs had 62.7% of the ball, against a season average of 62.8%.
They took 18 shots (9 on target) worth 2.73 xG, about 0.15 per shot; Ipswich Town had 11 shots worth 0.38 xG.

summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Ipswich Town's 4-2-3-1 (6 changes from the Leeds game, switching from 4-3-3).
The result matched the chances: 2.73 xG to 0.38.
On the main style measures this was a typical Spurs performance for the season: nothing moved more than 15% from their average.
Solanke was the biggest attacking threat (1.43 xG + xA).
